name: Transfeminism
summary: Transfeminism is a strand of feminism centred on trans women that holds their liberation to be bound up with the liberation of all women. It treats gender conformity and the binary sex system as tools of patriarchal control, defends each person's right to define their identity and decide about their own body, and wants trans life depathologised while medical care stays accessible. It is intersectional and coalitional, and its recent abolitionist wing links trans liberation to anti-capitalist and anti-carceral politics.
scope: Contemporary mainstream transfeminism as set out in Emi Koyama's Transfeminist Manifesto (2000-2001), Julia Serano's Whipping Girl (2007) and Wikipedia's survey of the tradition, plus the recent abolitionist strand of Nat Raha and Mijke van der Drift. Positions on bodily autonomy, gender, patriarchy, violence, reproductive rights, and medicine rest on Koyama; economic, foreign-policy and institutional answers are mostly inferred from the left, intersectional and abolitionist outlook and are low confidence. It excludes gender-critical feminism, which disputes trans women's inclusion.

sources.title: The Transfeminist Manifesto
sources.author: Emi Koyama
sources.usedFor: Core principles: self-definition, bodily integrity, patriarchy, violence, reproductive choice, depathologisation, intersectional self-critique.

sources.title: Transfeminism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: History, key thinkers, intersectionality, and the disputes with radical and lesbian feminism.

sources.title: Whipping Girl: A Transsexual Woman on Sexism and the Scapegoating of Femininity
sources.author: Julia Serano
sources.usedFor: Transmisogyny, oppositional and traditional sexism, and the case that feminism should include trans women.

sources.title: Trans Femme Futures: Abolitionist Ethics for Transfeminist Worlds (publisher description)
sources.author: Nat Raha and Mijke van der Drift
sources.usedFor: Abolitionist, anti-neoliberal and mutual-care strand of transfeminism; used only as an indicator for economic and institutional answers.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Koyama ties trans women's safety to cost and access of care and wants treatment made more accessible; Trans Femme Futures treats trans healthcare as a collective-care struggle, so guaranteed public care follows.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Koyama names poverty, low pay for women and employment discrimination as forms of economic violence against trans women, so a higher wage floor fits, though no wage policy is stated.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Pluto's blurb for Trans Femme Futures attacks the neoliberal order and favours collective provision; the rejection of market allocation is inferred, not argued directly.

public-ownership.rationale: Abolitionist, anti-neoliberal transfeminism favours common provision over market institutions, but public ownership of utilities is inferred rather than stated.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Raha and van der Drift speak of redistribution from rich to poor in a class-war frame, so higher taxes on wealth are inferred.

unions-good.rationale: Koyama wants to fight sexism and transphobia in the economic arena and treats employment discrimination as central; support for unions is inferred from that left coalition stance.

property-fundamental.rationale: Abolitionist and anti-capitalist currents give property no special sanctity, but transfeminist texts rarely address property rights; inferred.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Koyama's call to fight employment discrimination implies regulation of employers; wider corporate regulation is inferred.

cut-welfare.rationale: Koyama stresses poverty among trans women and economic violence that traps them with abusers; mutual-care ethics make cutting welfare contrary to the position.

worker-ownership.rationale: Collectives over institutions and anti-capitalism suggest sympathy for worker ownership, but no text discusses it; inferred.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Trans communities and abolitionist transfeminists distrust state policing and records that expose trans people; counterterror surveillance is an inference from that stance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Abolitionist ethics and bodily autonomy point to decriminalisation, but the sources do not discuss drug policy; inferred.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Adherents split between demanding protection from anti-trans abuse and distrusting state censorship that can be turned on marginal groups; texts do not settle it.

strong-leader.rationale: Coalition politics, collective organising and rejection of hierarchy make a leader bypassing gridlock alien to the position.

state-harmful.rationale: Abolitionist strands see state institutions as harmful, but Koyama works with shelters, medical and legal systems and seeks state recognition; adherents are split.

limit-guns.rationale: Koyama proposes self-defence training because of violence against trans women, yet most transfeminists favour gun control; no direct statement, so inferred.

empower-police-military.rationale: Koyama notes authorities rarely treat murders of trans women seriously, and Raha and van der Drift's abolitionist ethic rejects expanded police power.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Koyama and Serano's Excluded call for including sex workers and treat prostitution-linked violence as a safety issue rather than a crime to be policed; decriminalisation is the mainstream transfeminist view.

decide-locally.rationale: Collective, community-based organising favours local control, yet trans protections often depend on national law; texts do not address it.

rehabilitation.rationale: Abolitionist transfeminism rejects punitive imprisonment in favour of care and transformation, so rehabilitation over punishment fits.

traditional-family.rationale: Koyama attacks the patriarchal binary gender system and says a rigid gender hierarchy is the root problem, so fixed traditional family structures are rejected.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Transfeminism allies itself with queer liberation and attacks heterosexist patriarchy, so legal equality for same-sex couples is assumed even where marriage itself is criticised.

abortion-legal.rationale: Koyama's manifesto has a section arguing trans women's liberation is tied to women's right to choose and urges transfeminists to join reproductive choice organisations.

more-religion-public.rationale: The manifesto names religious authority among those who must not override bodily self-determination, so a larger public role for religion is rejected.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Koyama's postscript concedes feminism that ignores racism and classism is incomplete, and transfeminism aligns with intersectionality.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Koyama states that both sex and gender are socially constructed and that the distinction between them is drawn artificially for convenience.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Transfeminism is internationalist and challenges inherited gender norms; national tradition is not a concern of the texts, so inferred.

gradual-change.rationale: Koyama urges that trans women act now rather than debate, and favours small rebellions that destabilise the gender system, but she also seeks coalition inside existing institutions; leans against deference to them.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Decolonial and abolitionist transfeminists oppose border enforcement and trans migrants face its violence, but texts here do not address immigration levels; inferred.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Transfeminism uses international human-rights and WHO classification gains, yet decolonial strands are wary of universalising institutions; no settled view.

free-trade.rationale: Anti-neoliberal stance suggests scepticism of free trade, but the topic is not addressed; inferred.

nation-first.rationale: Coalition politics across groups and anti-colonial femme practices reject putting national interest first.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Anti-colonial and abolitionist commitments suggest suspicion of military intervention, but no text addresses it; inferred.

open-borders.rationale: Abolitionist and anti-colonial transfeminism favours free movement, but it is not a central stated demand; inferred.

limit-growth.rationale: Transfeminist texts do not address growth limits; anti-capitalist currents lean toward it but others do not.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Left anti-neoliberal currents back strong climate action, but the sources do not discuss climate; inferred.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Koyama is sceptical that medical technology alone settles trans liberation and stresses social change; techno-optimism is not part of the position.

expand-nuclear.rationale: No transfeminist source addresses nuclear power; adherents would split.

revolution-justified.rationale: Abolitionist transfeminism seeks transformative world-making beyond existing institutions, so some revolutionary change is acceptable though explicit endorsement is inferred.

experts-over-public.rationale: Koyama attacks the medical community for appointing itself arbiter of trans identity and insists that no medical authority override self-determination.

central-planning.rationale: Collectives over institutions suggests distrust of top-down planning, but economic design is not discussed; inferred.

socialized-markets.rationale: Anti-capitalist but non-statist currents would accept markets under collective ownership; inferred.

land-value-tax.rationale: No transfeminist source addresses land taxation; adherents would have no common view.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Redistribution from rich to poor implies taxing inheritance, but this is inferred from general class analysis.

basic-income.rationale: Koyama notes poverty traps trans women with abusers and mutual-care ethics favour unconditional support; basic income itself is inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Internationalist and anti-nationalist stance goes against protectionism, but trade is not discussed; inferred.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Adherents are split between redistribution through the state and distrust of state institutions; not addressed.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Anti-capitalism clashes with ownership-by-small-holders ideal as a goal, and the topic is not discussed; neutral.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Some abolitionist and anarchist-leaning strands would, but most transfeminists make no such demand.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; the free-market rationale for abolition is alien to a left, redistributive position.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised bodies setting wages is not a transfeminist idea and sits uneasily with collectives over institutions; inferred.

one-party-rule.rationale: Coalition politics and diversity-is-strength language contradict single-party rule.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Hereditary rule contradicts the rejection of hierarchy and inherited status at the core of the position.

democracy-best.rationale: Koyama works through coalition and public advocacy, but abolitionist strands distrust formal democracy and the statement's clause about bad voter choices is not addressed.

direct-votes.rationale: Participatory politics appeal, but texts do not take a side on referendums, and trans rights have been targeted by referendums.

workers-councils.rationale: Collective organising is favoured but councils as the basis of power are not discussed.

right-to-secede.rationale: The sources never address secession; adherents would split between anti-nationalism and sympathy for self-determination.

natural-rulers.rationale: Transfeminism rejects essentialist claims about innate fitness by gender and hierarchy generally.

political-violence-never.rationale: Koyama calls violence against trans people an emergency, but no source addresses political violence directly; most would reject pacifism as absolute.

war-builds-character.rationale: Care-centred, anti-colonial ethics reject glorifying war; inferred but strongly.

separate-church-state.rationale: The manifesto lists religious authority among those who must not impede decisions over our bodies, implying separation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Rejects religious authority over bodies and identities, so scriptural law is opposed.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Abolitionist ethics oppose policing as such, but private policing runs against collective care; inferred.

military-superiority.rationale: Anti-colonial, abolitionist outlook rejects pursuit of military superiority.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Intersectional, coalition politics reject an ethnically defined nation.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Class analysis is present but transfeminists emphasise gender, race and class together rather than class as the main driver.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Koyama calls for fighting economic disadvantage and rigid hierarchy, favouring more than formal opportunity, though equal outcomes is not stated.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Decolonial transfeminists draw on indigenous gender traditions and anti-colonial politics; land authority is inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Anti-colonial femme practices in Trans Femme Futures suggest support, but reparations are not discussed.

civilizational-union.rationale: Coalition across differences and rejection of essentialism oppose union by shared civilisation.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Mutual care and collective ethics oppose valuing self-interest as morally good.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The manifesto starts from each individual's right to self-definition and bodily integrity.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not addressed; transfeminism distrusts appeals to nature as justification for norms but takes no side on nature's value.

limit-population.rationale: Reproductive rights are framed as individual choice against coerced sterilisation, so state-limited population is opposed; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Not addressed; most adherents are not anti-industrial, so mildly negative.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Not addressed; transfeminism values medical technology access but also stresses social context.

human-enhancement.rationale: Koyama defends the right to modify bodies with hormones and surgery without authority interference, which implies bodily freedom to enhance them.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Distrust of institutions that define people from above suggests opposition, but not discussed; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Trans activists commonly value privacy against state and employer exposure, but encryption is not discussed; inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: Koyama aims to destabilise the normative gender system; restoring a lost order is opposed.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Transfeminism is explicitly principled; the manifesto starts from stated principles, so purely pragmatic policy judgment is disfavoured.

direct-action.rationale: The 1990s Transsexual Menace used direct action, and Koyama says we must act now rather than debate, though she also advocates coalition work in existing institutions.

means-match-ends.rationale: Koyama asks for friendly, cooperative coalition-building and Raha and van der Drift's mutual-care ethic aligns means with ends; not stated as a principle.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Not remotely part of the position; its care ethics are modern and urban.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Gender division of labour is criticised but its total abolition is not stated.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Mutual-care ethic points to need-based distribution, though not stated as such.

production-for-use.rationale: Anti-neoliberal, collective-care stance leans this way; inferred.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Class-war framing in Raha and van der Drift's work suggests it, but the claim is not stated in sources read.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Coalition politics and rejection of authoritarian hierarchy oppose dictatorial rule.

collective-farming.rationale: Farm organisation is outside the transfeminist literature read, so no position is recorded.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Anti-imperial framing leans toward it, but the sources never state the thesis.

taxation-theft.rationale: Redistributive, mutual-aid outlook rejects the claim.

harm-principle.rationale: Koyama insists on adult self-determination over body and identity, restricted only by harms to others, which matches a harm-based limit though she does not cite Mill.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Transfeminism is built on group coalitions and recognition of group-based oppression, though it begins from individual self-definition.

conscription.rationale: Bodily integrity against authority and anti-militarism oppose compulsory service; trans exclusion from military is a further factor.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Not a transfeminist idea; collective political voice and coalition are favoured.

state-as-business.rationale: Collective care ethics and anti-neoliberalism reject treating citizens as customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: Koyama links liberty to economic means, medical access and safety, not just non-interference.

media-academia-power.rationale: Transfeminists would see media and academia as hostile to trans people rather than dominant; not discussed in sources.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Koyama's critique of essentialism, and her endorsement of anti-racist critiques of white feminism, reject genetic claims about race and ability.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation through families and traditional bodies runs against the manifesto's rejection of patriarchal, gendered structures.

total-state.rationale: Opposes any authority overriding individual bodily and identity self-determination.

national-rebirth.rationale: Nationalist rebirth is alien to its coalition, anti-essentialist politics.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Anti-colonial and abolitionist ethics oppose it.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Koyama's rejection of hierarchy and inherited authority makes rule by personal oaths of lords incompatible with the position.

bound-labor.rationale: Opposes coercion and domination of labour; self-determination is the first principle.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Koyama argues medical classification of sex and gender is socially and politically constructed by those holding authority, and transfeminism draws on queer and trans studies.

universal-morality.rationale: Queer and decolonial strands challenge universalising claims; but Koyama's own rights language is universal-sounding, so mild.

single-common-good.rationale: The manifesto stresses diversity, difference and coalition among competing groups, rejecting a single universalised standpoint.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed; adherents hold divergent views.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Nothing in the sources covers diaspora return; adherents' anti-nationalism and migrant solidarity pull in different directions.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed; nationalist projects are unattractive to transfeminists.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Collectives over institutions suggests support; inferred.

school-vouchers.rationale: Marketised education runs against public-service preference, but not discussed.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Transfeminist economics is anti-austerity and wants public support for the poor, so a bar on deficit stimulus is disfavoured by inference.

economic-freedom.rationale: Anti-neoliberal view rejects the claim that political freedom depends on economic freedom in the market sense.

rule-by-example.rationale: Rejects authority resting on rulers' moral image and favours rights and collective action.

national-self-determination.rationale: Anti-colonial sympathies pull one way, anti-nationalism the other; not addressed.

force-without-un.rationale: Anti-militarist and anti-colonial ethic rejects unilateral force.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Not addressed; Koyama's emphasis on felt identity and lived experience means reason-only is not endorsed.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Solidarity across groups and abolitionist borders oppose restricting welfare to citizens.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Koyama's attention to employment discrimination against trans women makes work requirements punitive.

class-collaboration.rationale: The class-war language of Raha and van der Drift implies that employers and workers are not partners, though it is not stated as a rule.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not endorsed; transfeminism wants broad cultural inclusion rather than destruction of institutions.

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-imperial sympathies exist but no source discusses a front of dominated countries against the West.

workers-nation.rationale: Internationalist outlook opposes organising on national lines.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Koyama rejects the patriarchal binary gender system and institutional enforcement of rigid gender roles.

ban-interest.rationale: Not addressed; religious-style prohibition is not part of the position.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Koyama's critique of white women's racism in feminism and her acceptance of intersectionality oppose racial classification and segregation.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Some strands hold it, others seek legal gains from the state; split.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Left environmental outlook, but not discussed.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Opposes demands to conform to a dominant cultural norm, as it opposes conformity to gender norms.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy claims about immigration are rejected by a coalition politics that counts migrants as allies.

proportional-representation.rationale: Inclusive representation of minority voices is favoured, though not discussed.

national-mission.rationale: Anti-colonial outlook opposes missions to spread national government.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Koyama describes violence against women as a systematic function of the patriarchy and names heterosexist patriarchy the common target.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Distrust of institutions is present, but corruption claims are populist and not stated by sources.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Koyama condemns coerced sterilisation of less privileged women and nonconsensual intersex surgery, and insists on bodily self-determination.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Koyama notes authorities ignore murders of trans women, and abolitionist ethics demand accountability for state violence.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Koyama wants medical access and anti-discrimination action, which a minimal state would not give.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Koyama's account of racism within feminism and her coalition politics make discouraging mixed marriages plainly opposed.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The first principle is that each individual has the right to define identity and expect respect for it.

socialism-one-country.rationale: This Marxist-theory question is not discussed in any transfeminist source read.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Anti-colonial femme practices and decolonial trans feminism lean to yes; not directly stated for any state.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Uniform civil protections for trans people are favoured, but religious personal law is not discussed.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Opposes authority limiting individual choices of identity and religion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not addressed; opposes religiously motivated bans.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Rejects religious authority over bodies; supports secular schooling.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Opposes growth of state authority over individuals.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Consent and self-determination are core values, though applied to bodies more than states.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist trade aims are not addressed in the sources; no stated position.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Bodily integrity is central, but the property-centred, absolutist libertarian formulation is not adopted.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Mutual care and cooperation oppose a competitive view of progress.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Adherents split between wanting anti-trans groups restricted and distrusting state bans.

separated-powers.rationale: Constitutional design is not discussed; adherents mostly want protections against majorities but take no side.

vanguard-party.rationale: Coalition and collective organising, not disciplined vanguards.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Koyama says no authority should impede decisions over one's body; a domination frame fits, though republican theory is not cited.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Economic violence against trans women and mutual-care framing favour prioritising the poor.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing policy is not addressed in the sources; no position can be inferred with confidence.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Labour restrictions oppose the position's economic justice concerns.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Koyama attributes trans women's poverty to discrimination, pay gaps and transition cost, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Koyama says diversity is strength, not weakness, in the opening of the manifesto.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is not discussed in transfeminist texts.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Opposes suspension of protections, which historically fall on marginal groups.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price policy is not discussed; a pro-poor outlook suggests no objection but no support is stated.

party-controls-media.rationale: Opposes authority controlling information and expression.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Solidarity with migrants and abolitionist views on borders suggest opposing long waits, though this is inferred.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay of legislators is not discussed in the sources.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Not addressed; disciplined parties conflict with informal coalition politics.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split on EU-style bodies.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Concentrated executive power runs against the position.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not addressed; hierarchical religious rule disfavoured.

clerical-rule.rationale: Koyama denies religious authority any right to override bodily and identity decisions, so rule by clerics is opposed.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Anti-militarism leans yes, but not discussed.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Koyama defends expression and self-definition; moral censorship has been used against trans people.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Rejects concentration of power; not addressed.

recall-officials.rationale: Accountability is favoured but recall not discussed.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Anti-militarist outlook leans yes; not discussed.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Housing justice, but compulsory ownership is not their solution.

people-in-arms.rationale: An armed citizenry is not endorsed; the manifesto proposes self-defence training but the movement leans toward gun control.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Not part of the position, and trans people often flee rural hostility.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Border reunification is not discussed in any source read.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Transfeminism arises within academia and activism and values theory.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Decolonial transfeminists draw on non-Western gender traditions without ranking cultures, though they note some have oppressive features.

death-penalty.rationale: Abolitionist ethics in Trans Femme Futures reject punishment by state killing, and trans women are disproportionately victims of the justice system.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Directly supports challenging gender norms and informing young people.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The manifesto opposes religious authority impeding decisions about bodies and favours sex-ed and secular schooling; creationism teaching is opposed by inference.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Koyama and Serano's Sexed Up defend sexual autonomy and criticise sexual shaming, so legal restriction is opposed.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Anti-nationalist and pro-migrant commitments oppose ancestry-based citizenship, inferred from the coalition politics of Koyama's manifesto.

minority-language-support.rationale: Supports inclusion of minorities; not discussed.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemption claims have been used against trans people, so adherents resist them.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Koyama says there are as many ways of being a woman as there are women and favours a society free to make individual choices.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Anti-neoliberal and anti-colonial currents favour cancelling debts, though no source discusses it.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not addressed; anti-colonial transfeminism may agree but the sources do not state it.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitutional procedure is not addressed in transfeminist sources.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Koyama's whole politics rests on freedom of identity and bodily choice, so trading freedoms for growth is rejected.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Redistributive and anti-colonial commitments suggest support for aid, but no source states it.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Anti-militarist, abolitionist ethics oppose national nuclear arsenals by inference.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The method of choosing a head of state is not discussed.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Anti-neoliberal outlook disfavours insulating money from democratic control; inferred.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Anti-nationalist outlook disfavours historic-homeland claims; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Collective-care and anti-capitalist currents fit conditional property, but not stated.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Soviet history is not discussed in the transfeminist sources.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation doctrine is not addressed.

collective-defense.rationale: Not addressed; anti-militarist leaning conflicts with alliance obligations.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Opposes religious authority over bodies, so curbing religious institutions' public power fits; property aspects not addressed.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents have no shared view.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Anti-militarist and anti-nationalist views lean against force, but the topic is not discussed.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Autonomy arrangements are not addressed by transfeminist sources.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Divine or sacred rulers contradict the rejection of hierarchy and religious authority in the manifesto.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Redistribution from rich to poor, as implied by class-war framing in Raha and van der Drift, needs progressive rates.

character-from-environment.rationale: Koyama argues gender identities are constructed within social and cultural constraints, though Serano allows some innate traits, so only moderately yes.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy is not discussed; no position.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical constitutional theory is not discussed; no position.

leader-cult.rationale: Cults of personality run against Koyama's coalition politics and rejection of hierarchy.

equal-parenting.rationale: Koyama notes trans mothers would lose custody to abusers, so custody fairness matters, but a presumption of equal time is not discussed.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Intra-socialist doctrine is not addressed by transfeminist sources.

land-redistribution.rationale: Redistributive anti-capitalism implies support for redistributing land, but this is not stated in sources read.

refugee-return.rationale: Anti-colonial and migrant-solidarity politics suggest support for return, inferred; no source states it.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Ethnic-nationalist territorial claims are opposed by intersectional, anti-essentialist coalition politics.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The manifesto denies any religious authority the right to impede individual decisions about identity and body, so punishing leaving a religion is opposed.

women-must-cover.rationale: Koyama says women should be free to make their own decisions without guilt, and no authority should dictate bodies and expression.

common-currency.rationale: Monetary union is not discussed; no position.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority autonomy models are not discussed; no position.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Koyama urges fighting for rights within existing communities rather than withdrawing, though trans refugees are not discussed.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Not addressed; transfeminism emphasises ideas and identity as well.

ban-cartels.rationale: Anti-corporate-power leanings suggest support for antitrust, but the sources do not discuss competition policy.

no-bailouts.rationale: Opposes bailouts of banks but supports public aid for the poor; split.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Trans people are a minority needing legal protection from majorities.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Challenges gender hierarchy; parity bodies fit, though Koyama's focus is on who counts as a woman.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarkic blocs conflict with the internationalist, anti-colonial stance; inferred.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: A pro-labour, anti-neoliberal outlook would back binding standards, but no source states it.

moral-incentives.rationale: Incentive design is not discussed in sources read.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Not endorsed; Koyama's strategy is coalition and persistence.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The manifesto rejects inherited status hierarchies, and abolishing titles follows from that, though it is not discussed directly.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Decolonial strands oppose centring the nation's or civilisation's history; inferred.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Anti-colonial femme practices in Trans Femme Futures reject colonial tutelage.

patriotic-education.rationale: Teaching loyalty to flag and anthem conflicts with the position's rejection of enforced conformity and its anti-nationalism.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Koyama accepts that feminism ignoring racism is incomplete, favouring remedies.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Not discussed; transfeminist texts do not take a position on capitalist crisis theory.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Anti-colonial commitments oppose cultivating influence in former colonies.

delink-world-market.rationale: Dependency-theory strategies are not addressed in the sources.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: This Marxist-Leninist thesis is not addressed in the sources.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Koyama documents rampant employment discrimination against trans people and calls it a cause of economic violence.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Minority protections need entrenchment; implied by defence of self-determination.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Anti-colonial femme practices suggest sympathy, though treaty law is not discussed.

elective-rulers.rationale: Rejection of inherited authority implies choosing rulers by election, though not stated directly.

minority-veto.rationale: Coalition decisions bind members; but protections of minorities favoured.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The direct-action tradition suggests accepting resistance to lawless rulers, inferred.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Parliamentary sovereignty is not discussed; adherents often want courts to protect minorities.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed directly; care ethics lean yes.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is not discussed in sources read.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Mutual aid rather than paternalistic charity from privileged.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Koyama calls on trans women to act and join movements rather than withdraw.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Transfeminist sources read do not discuss mass culture as a pacifier, though they criticise media shaming of trans people.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Hegemony theory is not discussed in the sources read.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Anti-colonial framing implies agreement with unequal exchange, but no source states it.

native-born-offices.rationale: Native-born reservation conflicts with anti-nationalist and migrant-solidarity politics, by inference.

party-own-road.rationale: Communist party strategy is not discussed in transfeminist sources.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development strategy is not addressed; solidarity leanings give no clear direction.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Revanchist territorial demands run counter to the position's anti-nationalism.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Decolonial strands lean yes but not addressed.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Left politics, and the violence that fascism visits on trans people, favour anti-fascist constitutions; inferred.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Not discussed; anti-communist equivalence is not an issue the sources take up.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Denying slavery's role contradicts the anti-racist commitments Koyama endorses in her postscript.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Left, decolonial stance leans against keeping honours for condemned figures, but it is not discussed.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Koyama feared men's rights groups exploiting feminism, but does not oppose attention to men's hardship; split.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Koyama frames violence against women as systematic function of patriarchy while advocating services for trans men and women; symmetry not accepted.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Not addressed; decolonial strands are sympathetic.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Anti-militarist and abolitionist ethics oppose army political power.

paid-care-work.rationale: Care central to Trans Femme Futures; wages for care inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: Opposes imposed family obligations; many trans people lose family.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Economic nationalism is not addressed; no position.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Koyama notes trans women struggle to leave abusers; easy exit is favoured.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Participatory, collective politics suggest sympathy for recall, but sources do not discuss it.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Privatised pensions conflict with the anti-neoliberal, mutual-care stance, by inference.

single-official-language.rationale: Enforced linguistic uniformity matches the conformity pressures that the position resists.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Restricting foreigners' ownership conflicts with migrant solidarity, though property policy is not discussed.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Koyama's intersectional critique, but legal standard not addressed.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Consumer culture is not addressed; anti-capitalist leanings and body-image concerns give no clear answer.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Anti-militarist, anti-colonial ethic opposes covert arming of insurgents.

corporate-influence.rationale: Anti-neoliberal criticism of corporate power implies agreement, though lobbying is not discussed.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Opposes limits on NGOs; trans groups depend on international funds.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Koyama defends reproductive choice and opposes coerced reproduction, so state nudges toward childbearing are disfavoured.

residents-only-property.rationale: Housing justice politics oppose exclusionary purchase limits, but the topic is not discussed.

job-guarantee.rationale: Koyama's concern with employment discrimination; inferred.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Abolitionist ethics deny that law as such commands obedience, a view inferred from Trans Femme Futures.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Koyama's coalition politics condemn scapegoating of minorities, as trans people face.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Queer strands favour it, but trans activists fought for marriage recognition; split.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Transparency is not addressed directly; the pro-accountability stance suggests agreement.

local-production.rationale: Localism is not addressed in the sources read.

informal-organisation.rationale: Trans Femme Futures prefers collectives over institutions and mutual care, fitting small informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Not discussed; trans rights litigation uses both national and international law.

religious-nation.rationale: Defining the nation by religion is incompatible with the manifesto's rejection of religious authority over individuals.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Tributary hierarchy among states contradicts anti-hierarchy and anti-colonial commitments.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Redistribution across regions is more in line with the redistributive outlook, by inference.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Not discussed; anti-capitalist currents typically keep personal belongings private.

defeat-communism.rationale: Left politics rejects an anti-communist crusade, by inference; not discussed.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Service delivery models are not discussed in the sources.

religion-illusion.rationale: Not addressed; critical of religious authority but not of belief.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Anti-neoliberal and abolitionist texts present capitalism as a source of crises, not progress, though not argued in the pages read.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Koyama says transfeminism fights sexism and transphobia in economic arena; Raha and van der Drift call for world beyond neoliberal order.

socialized-care.rationale: Trans Femme Futures stresses collective care, which suggests public provision, though housework is not specifically discussed.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Linguistic purism conflicts with the stress on diversity and inclusion.

treaties-binding.rationale: Anti-colonial sympathies favour honouring treaties with indigenous nations, inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: Engineering demographic change in minority regions contradicts coalition politics.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Collectives and mutual care in Trans Femme Futures fit cooperative communities, but not common property as such.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Third-way positions are not taken up; the anti-capitalist leaning argues against calling both unsound.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Anti-essentialist, anti-nationalist outlook disfavours privileging historic ties, though not discussed.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Denial is contrary to commitment to truth about oppression; antisemitic conspiracy politics rejected.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Koyama names homophobia as target of violence and allies with queer liberation.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Suppression of independent organisations contradicts the coalition politics Koyama champions.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Koyama's rejection of religious authority and defence of expression oppose blasphemy punishment.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Anti-colonial femme practices reject governing colonies for the colonizer's benefit.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Islamic doctrine on jihad is not discussed in transfeminist texts.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Forcible removal for lacking religious law runs against rejection of religious authority and of political violence by clerics.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Koyama's postscript concedes feminism that fails to account for racism, classism and ableism is incomplete, and her manifesto addresses sexism and transphobia together.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Koyama's first principle is each individual's right to define identity and have society respect it, including protection against discrimination.

assisted-dying.rationale: Bodily autonomy implies support, but assisted dying is not discussed.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Transfeminism is a left project and rejects dismissing the left-right divide, though it is not stated.

alienated-labor.rationale: Anti-capitalist critique suggests agreement, but alienation is not discussed.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Essentialising a religion contradicts the position's anti-essentialism and anti-racism.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Koyama names religious authority among those who must not override people's decisions, so divine sources of authority are rejected.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Individual choice favoured over bans, though opposes religion in state.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Koyama addresses sexual and domestic violence and calls for accountability.

social-market-economy.rationale: Reformist social markets are not the position's ideal, but it also does not oppose them strongly.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Abolitionist ethics extend toward demilitarisation, inferred.

rich-first.rationale: Redistributive, mutual-care politics rejects letting some grow rich first.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Anti-militarist stance supports staying out of blocs by inference.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inherited office contradicts the rejection of inherited hierarchy.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutual credit is not discussed in sources.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Anti-austerity and anti-neoliberal views support refusing lender conditions.

property-franchise.rationale: Opposes exclusion of groups from political voice.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Wikipedia notes transfeminism overlapping with queer and decolonial theory, but no text says domination of nature matters here.

reification.rationale: Marxist commodity theory is not discussed in the sources.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Class critique of media power fits left politics, but is not addressed in the sources read.

racial-franchise.rationale: Racial limits on voting contradict Koyama's anti-racist coalition politics.

open-government-data.rationale: Open data is not discussed in sources read.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Targeting a religious minority is scapegoating, which transfeminist politics opposes in its own case.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Sortition assemblies are not discussed; participatory leanings suggest mild support.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Religious doctrine is not discussed in sources; progressive reform is plausible but inferred.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Anti-colonial and anti-nationalist commitments make unconsented annexation unlawful occupation by inference, though not stated.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Anti-militarist, anti-imperial ethics oppose a great power sending troops to keep an ally in the bloc.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The abolitionist and intersectional strand links trans liberation to anti-capitalism and sees wealth hierarchy as sustaining oppression; the liberty framing is inferred.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Transfeminism supports equal treatment regardless of sexuality, though abolitionists criticise the military as an institution; inferred.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Koyama defends each person's right to define their own identity and body, so state-imposed doctrine is inferred to be unwelcome; sources are silent.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The recent abolitionist wing links trans liberation to anti-carceral politics, but the mainstream tradition is less explicit; inferred.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The sources never address divided societies and nothing in the principles settles it.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The left, coalitional outlook favours mutual aid and public provision such as accessible medical care over charity alone; inferred.

term-limits.rationale: The sources never address term limits and nothing in the principles settles it.

vote-delegation.rationale: The sources never address vote delegation and nothing in the principles settles it.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The sources never address this and nothing in the principles settles it.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Transfeminism opposes patriarchal control and gender-based exclusion, so equal eligibility for religious office follows; the sources do not discuss it.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Koyama and Serano treat gender hierarchy and fixed gender roles as tools of patriarchal control, so husband authority is rejected.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from its intersectional, coalitional politics; migrants are not discussed in the sources.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from the anti-neoliberal, mutual-care outlook of the abolitionist strand.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents are split.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred: it treats imposed gender conformity as a tool of control, which uniformed national drilling would exemplify.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from its anti-carceral, anti-violence left outlook; not addressed directly.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from the same anti-imperial left outlook; not addressed directly.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred from its intersectional, anti-racist politics; not addressed directly.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the abolitionist strand's anti-capitalist and mutual-care politics; not stated directly.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Koyama defends bodily integrity and women's self-defence against violence is not ruled out, but the sources take no position on killing.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred: it holds identity to be self-defined and constructed rather than inherited.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Koyama and the Wikipedia survey criticise the binary sex system as a tool of patriarchal control and defend self-definition, though Serano also argues for the reality of bodily sex differences.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Transfeminism is coalitional and self-critical about trans, race and class differences, and rejects a fixed definition of woman that excludes trans women.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred: it opposes the cult of nation and sacrifice.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Inferred: its analysis is of patriarchy, sexism and material conditions rather than cosmic struggle.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents are likely split between secular and religious positions.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from its feminist aim of liberating all women; religion is not discussed in the sources.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from its intersectional anti-racism and anti-nationalism.

missingStatements.text: Medical treatment for gender transition should be available on the basis of the patient's informed consent, without a psychiatric diagnosis.
missingStatements.rationale: Koyama argues transsexuality is not an illness and that treatment should be made more accessible while depathologising gender identity disorder.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow medical-care question; gender-identity-recognition already covers recognising and protecting trans people.

missingStatements.text: Surgery to alter the sex characteristics of intersex children should be prohibited until they can consent.
missingStatements.rationale: Koyama calls genital surgery on intersex children inherently abusive because it violates bodily integrity without consent.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow intersex-medicine question that few other ideologies would take a side on; not worth a bank slot.

missingStatements.text: Women's shelters and rape crisis centres should serve people according to their gender identity.
missingStatements.rationale: Koyama urges that shelters and rape crisis centres accept trans women like any other women and that transfeminists help train them.

notes: Adherents differ on whether gender identity is innate (Serano allows some innate traits) or constructed (Koyama); this profile follows Koyama on social construction. The abolitionist wing (Raha, van der Drift) is more anti-state and anti-capitalist than the Koyama mainstream, so economic and policing answers carry low confidence.
